details:
Give creators more tools to check their worlds.
I've found people to use modded clients in-order to bug test and trial their worlds more efficiently, but modded clients can lead to bans.
The ability to fly, increase movement speed, and even clip through colliders all have uses when wanting to check a world is ready for public release. Large or complex worlds can take a long time to test to see if different aspects are working. 
"Does this button toggle properly?", "Is there a clipping issue at this corner of a race track?", "Is the lighting good while in a VR headset?". and even "How well does this world perform?" are questions that world creators can ask themselves and don't fully possess the tools needed to answer them efficiently.
I propose a variety of ideas that would all help world devs in their creations.
The VRC SDK could offer an asset, like a pickup tablet that would allow someone to enter "god mode", giving them toggles for flight, speed, clipping, even changing the render mode so the world dev could see a wireframe of the meshes around them. We've seen with the new physbones and contacts update that VRChat has a debug overlay for avatar interactions, it is possible for a dev to have access to this kind of tool while they are working on their world in-game. You could even have a debug UI that can pop up next to assets that are interactable or have scripts attached to them, allowing you to see if there is an error in the state as something is used over time.
It doesn't have to just be a tablet, you could instead have a mode in VRChat that allows you to do these features and more without a tablet instead. Like how you can test an avatar and only can see the model.
Or, another way, offering a more affective world test in unity. One that allows a more intuitive way of testing for VR users.
OH! And a way to test out worlds in both quest and pc mode. The Unity editor can only go so far. There are assets and shaders that don't show up properly in the Unity editor that can cause issues while in-game.
All I know is that it would be nice to have the features I see client users use for testing out worlds I create. I am sure others would also like the same.
title: Dev Tools for World Creators
